edges.description: Loss of functional FIBP perturbs intracellular modulation of FGF1/FGFR pathway signaling.
Altered intracellular FGF signaling derepresses somatic cellular proliferation.
Perturbed FGF-pathway modulation during nephrogenesis leads to variable renal and ureteric malformations.
Perturbed FGF-pathway modulation during embryonic brain development impairs neurogenesis and cognitive development.
Increased cellular proliferation drives postnatal proportionate somatic overgrowth.
Increased fetal cellular proliferation produces prenatal somatic overgrowth at birth.
Generalized cranial and somatic overgrowth produces macrocephaly.
Acral somatic overgrowth manifests with large hands, thumbs, and feet.
Hyperproliferative somatic signaling combined with dysplastic nephrogenic tissue predisposes to Wilms tumor.
Directly measures enhanced cellular proliferation and FIBP transcript reduction in patient-derived somatic cells.
edges.limitations: Dermal fibroblasts demonstrate the somatic hyperproliferation underlying overgrowth, whereas renal, neural, and cardiac developmental defects are not directly modeled in fibroblast monolayer culture.
